clinicalPearls: A spectrum of severe underdevelopment of the left heart structures, including the left ventricle, mitral and aortic valves and ascending aorta
The systemic circulation is duct-dependent, so infants collapse as the arterial duct closes
Presentation is with poor perfusion, shock and acidosis in the first days of life, often with only mild cyanosis initially
Survival before repair depends on maintaining ductal patency with prostaglandin and balancing pulmonary and systemic blood flow
Management is either staged single-ventricle palliation (Norwood pathway) or transplantation
It is one of the most serious forms of congenital heart disease and may be detected antenatally
reference.pathophysiology: In hypoplastic left heart syndrome the left ventricle cannot support the systemic circulation because of hypoplasia and inflow/outflow obstruction. Systemic perfusion depends on right ventricular output crossing the arterial duct, while pulmonary venous return must cross an atrial communication. As the duct constricts after birth, systemic output falls, producing shock and metabolic acidosis. The parallel circulation makes the balance between pulmonary and systemic flow critical, and excessive pulmonary flow can paradoxically worsen systemic perfusion.
additionalInvestigations: Assessment of ductal patency and atrial communication
Blood gas and lactate for perfusion
redFlags: Circulatory collapse as the duct closes
Rising lactate and acidosis indicating poor systemic perfusion
A restrictive atrial septum causing severe pulmonary congestion
Signs of inadequate systemic output despite treatment
reference.prognosis: Without intervention the condition is fatal; with staged surgical palliation or transplantation many children survive, though with significant long-term morbidity and the need for lifelong specialist care.
pitfalls: Mistaking early collapse for sepsis and not starting prostaglandin
Over-oxygenating and increasing pulmonary flow at the expense of systemic perfusion
Underestimating the need for early specialist transfer
